learningObjective: Given an elementwise kernel's per-element FLOP and byte cost, compute the arithmetic intensity and classify the kernel against a specific GPU's FP32 ridge point.

canonicalClaims.claim: For an elementwise kernel that reads and writes one tensor, arithmetic intensity equals per-element FLOPs divided by the sum of read bytes plus write bytes.
conditions: No cache reuse between elements (streaming access).
No fusion with adjacent ops that could reduce bytes moved.
nonImplications: Does not imply that increasing FLOPs per element (without changing bytes) will speed up the kernel unless AI crosses the ridge point.
Does not imply that switching to a lower-precision dtype always keeps the kernel memory-bound.

canonicalClaims.claim: An elementwise kernel with AI below the ridge point is memory-bound; the achievable ceiling is AI × HBM peak bandwidth.
conditions: Ridge point = peak compute / peak HBM bandwidth for the given precision.
nonImplications: Does not imply the actual throughput will match the ceiling; kernel implementation quality also matters.

misconceptions.claim: Increasing the number of FLOPs per element (e.g., adding more polynomial terms) will make an elementwise kernel compute-bound.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AI must cross the ridge point; going from 3 to 10 FLOPs per element only moves AI from ~0.4 to ~1.25 FLOP/byte, still well below A100's FP32 ridge of ~9.75 FLOP/byte.

misconceptions.claim: Arithmetic intensity should count only input bytes read (not output bytes written), because writes are asynchronous.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Writes consume HBM bandwidth on the write path; ignoring them undercounts memory traffic and overestimates AI.

misconceptions.claim: Elementwise kernels always saturate the SM math pipelines because they have perfect data-parallelism.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Data-parallelism enables occupancy, but throughput is capped by whichever roof (compute or memory) the AI intersects.

misconceptions.claim: Softplus is expensive enough per element that the FP16 version is compute-bound on A100.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP16 halves bytes per element but keeps FLOPs; AI doubles. Even at AI ≈ 2.5, we are still far below the FP16 Tensor-Core ridge point (~ 153 FLOP/byte) and below the FP16 non-TC ridge.

implementationFacts: A100 FP16 Tensor-Core ridge point ≈ 153 FLOP/byte
performanceScenarios: Activation functions (ReLU, softplus, GELU) applied outside of fusion boundaries are HBM-bound; fusion into a producing op is the main optimization lever.
